title: Muktinath Yatra Guide for Indian Pilgrims
meta_description: Muktinath yatra guide for Indian pilgrims: documents, ACAP permit, heli vs flight vs road, rituals at Muktinath and Kagbeni, altitude tips, cost and season.
summary: Muktinath (3,710 m) is reached from Kathmandu or Pokhara by helicopter in a morning, by flight via Jomsom in 4–6 days, or by road in 6–7 days. Indians need a passport or voter ID and an ACAP permit (NPR 1,000). Sleep in Jomsom, visit Muktinath and Kagbeni by day, and travel March–May or October–November.

sections.heading: Muktinath in brief
paras: Muktinath, Mukti Kshetra or Thiru Saligramam, is a Vishnu temple at 3,710 m in Nepal's Mustang district, counted among the 108 Divya Desams of Sri Vaishnava tradition. Behind the small pagoda shrine of Sri Muktinarayan, 108 brass spouts pour icy spring water, and pilgrims pass beneath them before bathing in the Lakshmi and Saraswati kunds. A short walk below, the Jwala Mai shrine holds a natural gas flame burning beside water, honoured by Hindus and Buddhists alike.

Most Indian families combine Muktinath with Pashupatinath in Kathmandu, and with Kagbeni, where the Kali Gandaki river yields Shaligram stones and where shraddha for ancestors is believed to carry special merit. A full yatra from Kathmandu takes anywhere from one day by helicopter to a week by road. This guide covers documents, routes, rituals, health and timing, based on how we run our own Muktinath departures.

sections.heading: Documents and permits for Indians
paras: Indian citizens do not need a visa for Nepal, but you must carry a valid passport or an original voter ID card (EPIC). These are the only two documents Nepal accepts as identity for Indian adults, and airlines, hotels and permit offices ask for them. Aadhaar, PAN cards and driving licences are not accepted. Children under 15 can travel with a birth certificate or school ID card alongside a parent, and those aged 15–18 with a school ID.

Muktinath lies inside the Annapurna Conservation Area, so every visitor over 10 needs an ACAP permit. Indians pay the SAARC rate of NPR 1,000, issued at the Nepal Tourism Board offices in Kathmandu or Pokhara with a photocopy of your ID and a passport photo. Buying it at a checkpoint costs double. Heli and package operators usually arrange it for you. Kagbeni village needs no extra permit, but going north of the Kagbeni checkpoint into Upper Mustang needs a separate restricted area permit.
list: Original passport or voter ID, plus two photocopies
Nepali rupees in cash for the Mustang leg; ATMs in Jomsom are unreliable
Indian ₹100 notes are widely accepted; rules on larger Indian notes have been restricted, so check current status before you travel
Travel insurance that covers altitude and helicopter evacuation

sections.heading: Three ways to reach Muktinath
paras: Your choice comes down to time, budget and the health of the oldest traveller in your group. Helicopters are fastest and gentlest on the body because you spend only an hour at altitude, but cost the most. The flight via Jomsom is the classic middle option, with two nights in Jomsom and visits to Kagbeni and Marpha, but the small planes are frequently delayed. The road is cheapest and immune to flight cancellations, but long, dusty drives tire seniors and landslides disrupt it in the monsoon.

sections.heading: Rituals at Muktinath and Kagbeni
paras: At Muktinath, the usual order is snan under the 108 spouts, a dip in the two kunds, then darshan of Sri Muktinarayan, offering tulsi, flowers and sweets, followed by the Jwala Mai flame and a donation to the nuns who care for the temple. Bathing fully is optional; priests accept sprinkling the water on the head, and we advise seniors, children and anyone with heart or blood pressure problems to do only that. The water is near freezing all year.

At Kagbeni, families walk to the confluence of the Kali Gandaki and Jhong Khola to search for Shaligram in the gravel and to perform shraddha, pinda daan or tarpan with a local priest. Bring the names of three generations of ancestors and your gotra. The dakshina is usually agreed in advance at around ₹2,500–6,000 per family. Plan Kagbeni for the morning or early afternoon, before the strong valley wind makes the riverbank cold and dusty.
list: Carry a towel, a full change of clothes and a plastic bag for wet clothes
Leave leather belts and wallets outside the inner shrine
Photography of the main murti is not allowed
Walk clockwise around Buddhist shrines and prayer wheels

sections.heading: Altitude and health for seniors
paras: At 3,710 m there is roughly 35 % less oxygen per breath than at sea level, a little higher than Kedarnath. Most healthy visitors feel only breathlessness on the steps, but headaches, nausea and poor sleep are common if you go up fast and stay overnight. Our rule is simple: sleep in Jomsom at 2,720 m and visit Muktinath as a day trip. Helicopter visitors spend about an hour at the top, which most people tolerate well.

Walk slowly, drink 3–4 litres of water a day, avoid alcohol and keep warm. People with heart disease, severe asthma or COPD, uncontrolled blood pressure, recent surgery, and pregnant women should consult a doctor before travelling, and may be advised to stop at Jomsom. Some doctors prescribe acetazolamide as a preventive; take it only on medical advice. Horses and porters can carry those who cannot manage the 15–20 minute climb from Ranipauwa to the temple.

sections.heading: Best time for the yatra
paras: March to May and late September to November give clear mornings, daytime temperatures of 10–20 °C at Muktinath and the most reliable flights. May and June are busiest because of Indian school holidays, so book flights and hotels early. July and August bring little rain to Muktinath itself, but cloud cancels Jomsom flights for days and landslides block the road from Pokhara. From December to February, nights fall to −10 °C, many Ranipauwa hotels close and snow can shut the road above Jomsom for days.

sections.heading: Packing list for Muktinath
paras: Even in May, mornings at Muktinath can be near freezing and the afternoon wind is cold and dusty. Pack in layers and keep bags light: the Pokhara–Jomsom plane allows only about 10–15 kg checked and 5 kg hand luggage per person.
list: Warm jacket, fleece or sweater, thermal inners, woollen cap and gloves
Comfortable walking shoes and slip-on sandals for the temple
Sunglasses, sunscreen, lip balm and a scarf or mask for dust
Towel and quick-dry clothes for bathing
Personal medicines, plus paracetamol, ORS and motion-sickness tablets
Puja items you prefer to bring from home, and a small bottle for holy water
Power bank and torch; electricity can be irregular

faqs.a: From Kathmandu, a 5-night yatra by flight via Jomsom costs from about ₹54,000 per person in 3-star hotels, and by road from about ₹32,000. Helicopter day trips cost ₹52,000–65,000 per seat from Pokhara and ₹89,000 or more from Kathmandu. Add your travel to Kathmandu or the border. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is a passport required for Muktinath?
faqs.a: Indian citizens need either a valid passport or an original voter ID card; no visa is required. Aadhaar, PAN and driving licences are not accepted as identity in Nepal for flights, hotels or permits. Children under 15 can use a birth certificate or school ID with a parent.

faqs.q: Can we go to Muktinath by train from India?
faqs.a: There is no railway to Muktinath. The nearest Indian railheads are Gorakhpur for the Sunauli border and Raxaul for Birgunj. From Sunauli, Pokhara is about 8 hours by road and Muktinath another 8–10 hours by jeep. Many pilgrims take the train to Gorakhpur and continue by road.

faqs.q: How many days are needed for Muktinath yatra?
faqs.a: By helicopter, one day from Kathmandu or a morning from Pokhara. By flight via Jomsom, 5–6 days from Kathmandu including Pashupatinath, Pokhara and Kagbeni. By road, 6–7 days from Kathmandu, or 4–5 from Pokhara. Add a buffer day for flight delays.

faqs.q: Is Muktinath safe for elderly parents?
faqs.a: Yes, with sensible planning. Fly rather than drive if possible, sleep in Jomsom rather than Muktinath, walk slowly and use a horse for the final climb if needed. Get a medical check first. Those with serious heart or lung conditions should consult a doctor and may be advised against going to 3,710 m.

faqs.q: Which month is best for Muktinath darshan?
faqs.a: April, May, October and November are the best months, with clear skies and reliable flights. March and late September are also good. Avoid July and August if travelling by flight or road because of monsoon disruptions. Winter is possible but very cold, with some hotels closed.

faqs.q: Do we need a guide for Muktinath?
faqs.a: No licensed guide is legally required for Muktinath by road, flight or helicopter, as it is not a restricted area. A guide is useful for permits, jeep bookings, priest arrangements at Kagbeni and helping seniors at the temple. Trekking into the conservation area on foot now requires a licensed guide.

faqs.q: Can we stay overnight at Muktinath?
faqs.a: Yes, Ranipauwa below the temple has many simple hotels used by pilgrim groups. However, sleeping at 3,700 m increases the risk of altitude sickness, especially after a quick ascent. We recommend sleeping in Jomsom, 1–1.5 hours below, unless you are fit and have acclimatised gradually.

faqs.q: Is food available for vegetarians at Muktinath?
faqs.a: Yes. Hotels in Jomsom and Ranipauwa serve pure vegetarian Indian and Nepali food, such as dal, rice, roti, sabzi and paneer, and many cook without onion and garlic on request. Carry some dry snacks from home for the jeep ride and flight delays.
